__doc: MASTER TUNING FILE. Every number the simulation uses lives here. Edit values, save, and the app hot-reloads. Keys starting with __ are comments and are ignored by the game.

playerGeneration.__doc: Controls how new players are created (free agents, youth prospects, rivals).
playerGeneration.__ageRange: Fortnite is a young scene. 13-16 = prospect, 17-21 = prime, 22+ = veteran.
playerGeneration.__attrFloor: No attribute may go below/above these, even after strengths and weaknesses are applied.
playerGeneration.__strengthCount: CORE RULE: every player gets 2-3 spiked attributes and 2-3 tanked ones so nobody is well-rounded. Raising these numbers makes players more extreme and specialised.
playerGeneration.__archetypeBiasStrength: Multiplier on the per-archetype attribute bias in archetypes.json. 0 = archetype has no effect on ratings.
playerGeneration.__noiseSigma: Random wobble added to every attribute at creation.

potentialGapByAge.__doc: Hidden Potential = current overall + a gap. Younger players get bigger gaps (more room to grow). Ages between the listed ones are interpolated.

playerGeneration.__ego: Hidden. High ego drags duo synergy down. Star players tend to have more of it (see egoStarBonus).
playerGeneration.__egoStarBonus: Ego points added per overall point above 70. Stars are divas.

salary.__doc: Weekly salary in dollars. salary = base * exp(growth * (overall - pivot)) + potentialBonus * (potential - overall)

contract.__doc: Contract length in weeks offered by free agents, and buyout cost for players at rival orgs.
contract.__buyoutMultiplier: Buyout = weekly salary * this. Only applies to players already signed to a rival org.

simulation.__doc: THE MATCH ENGINE. It reads the 29 SUB-STATS directly - the old 11-attribute bridge is gone. See MATCH-SIM.md for the shape of a match. Every check below is described by a weight set of SUB-STAT ID -> weight, split into `raw` (the ability being tested, weights should sum to 1) and `fighting` (which Fighting sub-stats decide how much of that raw ability actually converts).
simulation.__duelScale: Logistic softness of every contested check. WinChance = 1/(1+e^-(myPower-theirPower)/duelScale). LOWER = skill matters more and upsets are rarer. HIGHER = more chaos.
simulation.__lobbySigma: Spread of opponent strength inside a lobby. Higher = you meet more sweats AND more bots.
simulation.__SCALE_NOTE: IMPORTANT: lobbyRating in tournaments.json is on the TEAM POWER scale, not the individual rating scale. TWO players averaging 50 OVR make a duo worth roughly 61 team power, because the stronger player carries (teamAggregation) and chemistry adds on top. Rule of thumb: a duo COMPETES when lobbyRating is about 10 below its strength number, and DOMINATES about 25 below. The Dashboard shows each duo strength, so compare that with the lobby rating shown on the Tournaments screen.

lobby.__doc: The shape of one competitive lobby.
lobby.__teams: A comp duos lobby is 100 players = 50 duos, so every placement in the game is a placement out of 50 and the scoring table in tournaments.json is written for that. Move this and the scoring table has to move with it.

survivors.__doc: How many teams are still alive at the END of each stage of a match. When you die, your placement is drawn from the band the lobby was actually in at that moment - placements are never free-floating random numbers, which is why dying off the drop is always a bottom-ten finish and dying in the last mid-game zone is always a top-25 one.
survivors.__afterZones: One entry per mid-game zone. Add a fourth number and the match grows another zone - the engine reads the length of this array.

teamAggregation.__doc: How the two players in a duo combine into ONE team number, per CATEGORY. 0.0 = plain average (BOTH of them need it). 1.0 = only the better player matters (a specialist carries the duo). When one player is DOWN, the survivor's own numbers are used unchanged - which is exactly why a lopsided duo is fragile.

fightingMultiplier.__doc: THE FIGHTING CATEGORY IS A MULTIPLIER, NOT ANOTHER ADDITIVE STAT. Any check that carries a `fighting` weight set converts its raw power around the neutral 50 line: above 50 the surplus is multiplied, below 50 the deficit is divided. Fighting decides how much of a duo's aim and mechanics they actually get to use in a real fight.
fightingMultiplier.__perPoint: mult = 1 + (fightScore - 50) * perPoint. Fighting 90 gives 1.28x, Fighting 20 gives 0.79x.

fatigue.__doc: Long sessions grind players down. Applied from match freeMatches+1 onwards.
fatigue.__perMatch: Raw fatigue points added per match after the free ones.

resistance.__doc: There is no Stamina sub-stat in the tree, so endurance is read off the head instead. Weights are normalised into a 1-99 endurance number.

fatigue.__resistanceScale: At endurance 99 a player keeps only (1 - 0.9) of the fatigue penalty.

sensitivityByCategory.__doc: Which parts of a player fall off when they are tired. 1.0 = full fatigue hit, 0 = immune. Hands go first; reads barely move.

consistencyModel.__doc: Per-match form roll, rolled separately for EACH player. Low Consistency = boom or bust.
consistencyModel.__consistencyScale: sigma = baseSigma * (1 - consistency/99 * consistencyScale). At consistency 99 the roll is nearly flat.
consistencyModel.__perCheckJitter: Extra small noise on each individual duel so the same match never plays out identically.

mental.__doc: WHEN each mental sub-stat is allowed to matter. Every one is two-way: below the anchor is a penalty, above it is a bonus. This is what stops Mental being a flat stat you can ignore.

pressure.__perPoint: Power per point of team Under Pressure away from the anchor, applied ONLY in a pressure moment.
pressure.__lastMatchesOfSession: The closing games of a session are a pressure moment - that is where a run is won or thrown away.
pressure.__endgameFromPlacement: Every circle from this placement down is a pressure moment.

clutch.__perPoint: Power per point of Clutch away from the anchor. ONLY applied while that player is the last one alive - a real 1v2. It never touches a normal two-up fight.
clutch.__saveChance: Max chance a lost endgame check is survived anyway, scaled by how far Clutch sits above the anchor.

tilt.__badPlacement: Finishing worse than this counts as a disaster game and tilts the duo for the NEXT match.
tilt.__basePenalty: Power lost in the following match at Tilt Resistance 1. At Tilt Resistance 99 almost none of it lands.

bigStageNerve.__perPoint: Power per point of team Big Stage Nerve away from the anchor. APPLIED ONLY AT EVENTS FLAGGED lan:true IN tournaments.json - at every other event Big Stage Nerve is ignored completely. This is why a 15-year-old prodigy can farm cash cups and still fold at the Grand Final.

synergy.__doc: Duo chemistry. The result is a flat plus/minus applied to every performance sub-stat all session long.
synergy.__commsWeight: Points of synergy per point of the duo's average Communication above 50.
synergy.__iglWeight: Points of synergy per point of the BEST Decision Making in the duo above 50. Somebody has to make the calls.
synergy.__egoPenaltyWeight: Synergy lost per point of average Ego above 50.
synergy.__egoTopDogPenalty: Extra penalty per point of the HIGHEST ego in the duo above 50. One diva ruins a lockerroom.
synergy.__gamesTogetherBonus: Max bonus once the duo has played gamesTogetherFull matches together. Ramps on a square-root curve.
synergy.__adaptivityRampScale: How much Adaptivity shortens that ramp. At average Adaptivity 99 the duo gels after (1 - 0.45) of gamesTogetherFull; at 1 it takes (1 + 0.45) of it.

composition.__doc: Bonus or penalty for the mix of archetypes in the duo.
composition.__bothSameArchetype: In a duo an archetype clash bites harder than it did in a trio - there is no third player to cover the gap.

downedPartner.__doc: DUOS ARE TWO PEOPLE. Losing a fight usually knocks ONE of them, not both, and the survivor plays on alone until they can rebuild. This block is what makes a duo more than one blended stat line.
downedPartner.__powerPenalty: Power lost on every check while a player is down. A 1v2 is a losing position and should feel like one.
downedPartner.__wipeChanceOnLoss: Chance that losing a fight kills BOTH players outright instead of knocking one of them. Reset Timing and Movement pull it down - good players get out.
downedPartner.__wipeSkillScale: wipeChance is scaled by (1 - (wipeReducedBy power - 50)/50 * wipeSkillScale).
downedPartner.__soloWipeChance: Chance the last player alive simply dies when they lose a check, instead of escaping. Much higher than the duo number - there is nobody to trade for you.

reboot.__doc: Getting the partner back. Only possible before the final circles, and only if the survivor is still alive at the end of the stage.
reboot.__skillScale: Chance is baseChance scaled by (1 + (power - 50)/50 * skillScale).
reboot.__notBelowPlacement: No reboots once the lobby is down to this many teams - the vans are gone and there is nowhere safe to res.

drop.__doc: PHASE 1. Where they land and whether they have to fight for it. This is the Offspawn category's moment.
drop.__contestChanceByStrategy: Chance the chosen POI is actually fought over. Strategy is set per duo in the UI.
drop.__aggroContestBonus: Added to contest chance per aggressive player in the duo (mech_carry, fragger, prodigy).

power.__doc: A drop fight is decided with whatever you picked up in the first fifteen seconds, which is why the Offspawn sub-stats dominate it and Piece Control barely features.

drop.__winMats: Mats PER PLAYER. Everything in the engine is per player now - a lone survivor only carries their own.
drop.__winLootBonus: Added to the loot number in phase 2 when a contested drop is WON - you cleared the POI, so you have the whole POI. This is the payoff that makes contesting worth the risk of a bottom-ten finish.

health.__doc: PER-PLAYER HP. Until build step 4 a player only had shield, and any damage past it simply vanished - you could take 40 chip damage in six zones running and walk into the endgame untouched. Now damage eats shield first and then HP, HP is carried from phase to phase, and a player who runs out of it goes down.

healPerZone.__doc: What a duo puts back on out of minis and slurp in a zone they got through QUIETLY. A zone with a fight in it buys no healing at all - that is the whole point, and it is why a duo that takes every fight arrives in the endgame on low HP while a zone player arrives full. Measured first: damage runs about 37 a match on average and 85 at the 90th percentile, so healing much above this makes HP decorative.

health.__healPerZone_history: These were 14/22 and applied on EVERY zone including ones with a fight, which handed a duo roughly 216 free HP across a match against 37 average damage. The result was zero HP knockouts in 5400 test matches - the whole health system was decoration. Conditional and smaller is what makes it bite.

healAfterWonFight.__doc: Cracking somebody usually means their shield. This is the ONLY healing a fight zone gives, and it goes to the winner.

fightDamage.__doc: YOU DO NOT WIN A BOX FIGHT FOR FREE. Damage taken in a fight the duo WON. Losing a fight is already paid for through RESET_DAMAGE and the casualty rules, but until this existed winning cost nothing at all, so a duo could take ten fights and reach the endgame untouched - which is why HP was decoration. This is the number that makes a W-key duo arrive in the endgame hurt and a zone duo arrive full.

health.__knock: A player whose HP reaches zero is KNOCKED, exactly as if they had lost a fight - the partner plays the 1v2 and may rebuild them. That is a new way to lose a player as of step 4, and it is the point: chip damage now has to be respected.

loot.__doc: PHASE 2. Drop Accuracy and Resource Mgmt turn into mats and shield. Positioning and Rotation decide the first rotate.
loot.__matsPerLootStat: Mats per point of the team's loot number below. Per player.
loot.__matsCap: Per player. Fortnite caps each material at 500; a comp player carries somewhere around 500-700 usable mats into a late game.

tiers.__doc: THE GUN YOU ACTUALLY CAME AWAY WITH, carried from the drop through the whole match. The loot number below (drop accuracy, resource mgmt, fifty-fifties) picks the tier; winning a contested drop bumps it, losing one drops it. As of build step 4 the tier is TRACKED but does not yet change a fight - BAD_LOOT_PENALTY is wired in at step 5, and `powerByTier` is the number it will read.
tiers.__thresholds: Loot number needed to reach each tier; anything under `green` is grey. Set against the MEASURED spread of the loot number across every standard of player - its 5th percentile is about 40, its median 75 and its 95th about 118 - so the tiers come out roughly 15/20/25/25/15 percent. The first guess at these (82/72/62/52) made two thirds of all drops gold and only 3% blue, which told you nothing.
tiers.__contestWinBonus: Added to the loot number when you clear a contested POI - you own everything on it.
tiers.__contestLossPenalty: Taken off when you lose the fifty-fifty. Losing the chest race means a worse gun, not death.
tiers.__powerByTier: STEP 5. Power a fight gains or loses from the loot in hand, blue being neutral. Nothing reads this yet.

rotatePower.__doc: No `fighting` set: a rotate is a map decision, not a fight. Fighting cannot save you from a bad route.

loot.__rotateDifficultyBonus: Added to lobby rating for the rotate check. Bad rotates punish everyone.
loot.__failDeathChance: Chance a blown rotate turns into a fight you did not choose, resolved with the mid-game weights and the downedPartner rules.
loot.__thirdPartyElimChance: If you survive a bad rotate you sometimes trade. Chance of picking up an elim anyway.

midGame.__doc: PHASE 3. One pass per zone (see lobby.survivors.afterZones): the fights you CHOOSE, then the pressure you cannot avoid, then a chance to rebuild.
midGame.__disengageShieldCost: Shield lost when a lost mid-game fight ends in breaking contact rather than a knock. This used to be hard-coded in sim.ts; it moved here when the modifier pipeline went in, with the same value, so nothing changed.
midGame.__optionalFightChance: Base chance per zone that the duo goes looking for a fight.
midGame.__aggroFightBonus: Added per aggressive player in the duo (mech_carry, fragger, prodigy).
midGame.__fightSelectionScale: Opponent power REMOVED per point of team Fight Selection above 50, but only in a fight the duo CHOSE. Good fight selection is not winning more fights, it is picking easier ones - so it never helps in a forced fight.
midGame.__fightSelectionSkipScale: Chance per point of Fight Selection above 50 that a bad-looking fight is declined outright.
midGame.__lowMatsPenalty: Power lost in a fight while under lowMatsThreshold mats.

zonePower.__doc: Unavoidable pressure on the way in: shrinking zone, teams stacking your side, third parties. Nobody can rotate around these, which is what stops a passive duo reaching every endgame. THIS IS THE MAIN DIAL FOR HOW HARD IT IS TO MAKE TOP 15.

midGame.__zoneDeathChance: Chance a lost zone-pressure check turns into a real fight rather than chip damage. That fight then runs through the downedPartner rules, so it usually costs a player before it costs the game.
midGame.__zoneDifficultyRamp: Lobby rating added per zone survived. Every zone the lobby is a little better than the last one, because the bad teams are already dead.

endGame.__doc: PHASE 4. From the top 15 down to the win, one check per circle.
endGame.__circles: How many teams are still alive after each closing circle, starting from the 15 that reached the endgame. SEVERAL teams die per circle early on and then it thins out, which is what a real endgame looks like - it is not fifteen consecutive 1v1s. One entry per check; the last entry must be 1.
endGame.__difficultyRamp: Lobby rating added per circle survived. The last few circles are all sweats.
endGame.__matsSavedByBuildEfficiency: Mats per circle saved per point of team Build Efficiency above 50. This is the sub-stat that decides whether a duo is still building in zone 9.

matsPressure.__doc: RUNNING OUT OF MATS IN THE FINAL ZONES SHOULD KILL YOU. This used to be a cliff: no penalty at all until a player hit exactly zero, then a big one. That let a duo walk into the endgame on 40 mats and feel nothing until the very last circle. It is now a RAMP - the penalty grows the further below `comfortable` you are, so arriving short is punished from the first circle.
matsPressure.__comfortable: Mats per player entering a closing circle that count as enough. At or above this there is no penalty at all. The design brief asks that entering zone 8 under 100 mats usually kills you, and this is that number - `npm run verify:state` measures whether it actually does.
matsPressure.__penaltyAtZero: Power lost by a player on ZERO mats. Between 0 and `comfortable` the penalty scales straight down to nothing.
matsPressure.__curve: Above 1 the penalty bites harder as you approach empty - 60 mats hurts a little, 10 mats hurts a lot. Set to 1 for a straight line.

endGame.__elimChancePerCircle: Chance of picking up kills in a circle you survive. Across a full endgame run this is most of a winning duo's elim count.

aiField.__doc: The other 200-3000 duos on the leaderboard. Running a full five-phase match for every one of them would take seconds per tournament, so instead each of their matches is drawn as a PLACEMENT and an ELIM COUNT and then scored through the SAME points table you are - which means changing the scoring table moves their totals exactly like it moves yours.
aiField.__strengthSigma: Spread of rival duo strength around the tournament lobby rating, on the TEAM POWER scale (roughly 1.4 points per point of player OVR).
aiField.__strengthSkew: Open lobbies are not symmetric - a few monsters and a very long tail of teams who should not be there. Negative values lengthen the weak tail. 0 = a plain bell curve.
aiField.__slopePerRatingPoint: How much one point of team strength above the lobby shifts a duo's placement roll, in logit units. At 0 every duo places uniformly at random, which is exactly what a lobby of identical teams should look like. THIS IS THE DIAL FOR HOW MUCH SKILL BEATS LUCK ON A LEADERBOARD.
aiField.__elimPerQuality: Extra expected elims for a duo that wins the game, on top of elimBase. Across a 50-team lobby the field should average about 2 elims a game, because 98 of the 100 players die.

economy.__weeklyOverhead: Fixed running cost of the org per week, on top of salaries.
economy.__fansPerReputationPoint: Fans drift toward fansPerReputationPoint * reputation^fanReputationExponent each week. Fans are where most of your income comes from, so this is the master income dial.
economy.__fanReputationExponent: Below 1.0 this gives diminishing returns, so a famous org does not print infinite money. Set to 1.0 for a straight line.
economy.__baseSponsorIncomePerWeek: Flat weekly sponsor money every org gets, even at zero reputation. This is the floor that keeps a new org alive while it builds a following.
economy.__sponsorIncomePerFanPerWeek: Weekly sponsor money = fans * this * (1 + reputation/100). Prize money is the jackpot; sponsors are what actually pay the salaries, exactly like the real scene.
economy.__reputationDecayPerWeek: Reputation you lose per week if you do nothing. Stay relevant.

reputationPerTournament.__doc: Reputation gained by finishing in the top X percent of a tournament, before region and tier multipliers.

economy.__bankruptcyGraceWeeks: Weeks you may run a negative balance before the org folds (game over).

org.__doc: Roster limits and the quality of players you start with / find on the market.
org.__rosterLimit: Maximum players under contract at once. Four duos worth, plus subs.
org.__duoLimit: Maximum duos you may field. The game mode is DUOS - two players per team.
org.__startingPlayers: How many players you begin with. Three means one duo plus a sub, so you start with a real roster decision.
org.__startingPlayerRating: Average quality of the players you begin with. Raise this for an easier start.

marketRating.__doc: Quality of players appearing on the free agent / transfer market. Most are journeymen, a few are stars.
marketRating.__prospectChance: Chance a market player is generated young, with lower ratings but a much higher hidden potential.

scouting.__doc: Unknown players show as RANGES. Scouting narrows them.
scouting.__pointsPerWeek: Scout actions available each week. Refills on week advance.
scouting.__uncertaintyByLevel: Plus/minus shown on each attribute at scout level 0,1,2,3,4. Level 4 = exact numbers.

hiddenRevealLevel.__doc: Scout level required before hidden traits are shown at all, and even then only as a vague band.

scouting.__poolRefreshWeeks: How often unsigned free agents are rotated out for fresh faces.

progression.__doc: How players grow and decline week to week, independent of training.
progression.__declinePerWeek: Attribute points lost per week per year of age past declineStartAge.
progression.__matchExperienceGain: Passive growth per match played, scaled by remaining potential.
